name: israel

events.event: Israeli Culture Minister Miki Zohar threatened to revoke the citizenship of filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor.
Israeli Culture Minister Miki Zohar accused the creators of the 'NAZA' documentary of a 'betrayal of the state' and self-loathing.
Israeli forces have killed 1,107 Palestinians in the West Bank since October 7, 2023.
Israeli forces struck a car in Gaza City's Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood, killing two Hamas engineers and wounding 13 people.
Israel's military chief Eyal Zamir ordered the military prosecutor to examine and advance possible legal measures concerning the film Naza and those involved.
The film Naza won the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival on Saturday.
The film Naza received a 25-minute standing ovation when it was screened at the Venice Film Festival.
The film Naza's official synopsis details the systems behind Israel's calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza.
Israeli forces set up at least 925 movement obstacles, including roadblocks and unmanned checkpoints, in the West Bank by the end of 2025.
International Organization for Migration estimates about 330,000 people remain displaced in Lebanon.
UNHCR's Nadine Mazloum says displacement patterns remain highly fluid and often reversible.
Hezbollah responded to Israeli attacks on Lebanon on March 2, 2026.
Israel currently occupies more than 50 villages in southern Lebanon.
The offensive in southern Lebanon has killed more than 4,380 people.
A June framework agreement between Israel and Lebanon did not stop Israeli attacks on southern Lebanon.
More than 810,000 people in Lebanon have returned home or to nearby places since the 2024 ceasefire.
Soujoud Ramadan returned to her village of Froun after the 2024 ceasefire.
The International Organization for Migration reported 80 percent of displaced people are in five districts.
The International Organization for Migration reported 17,566 registered displaced people live in collective sites.
The International Organization for Migration reported 75 percent of displaced people are living in rented accommodation.
Norwegian Refugee Council's Maureen Philippon said she passed through villages with not one single standing wall.
Norwegian Refugee Council's Maureen Philippon said many locals from southern villages had to flee again after the resumption of attacks.
Israeli forces killed a pregnant Palestinian woman in Gaza.
Israeli quadcopters were deployed to track and target civilians in Gaza City.
Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich approved more than 3,000 homes in the E1 settlement project.
West Virginia assistant football coach Noel Devine was arrested on a felony strangulation charge.
Israeli forces targeted two Hamas engineers, Hassan Ali Abu Nada and Abd al-Rahim Ahmad Khalil Khawa, accusing them of weapons production.
Israeli forces killed two teenagers during a military raid in al-Mughayyir, east of Ramallah, in early September.
Israeli forces demolished every home in Khirbet al-Tabban, displacing about 70 people, including 30 children, in early September.
Israeli forces killed a 14-year-old student named Aws in al-Mughayyir on April 21.
Israeli forces forcibly displaced at least 75 Palestinian communities and 33,000 Palestinians from refugee camps in the northern West Bank.
Israeli forces established at least 1,070,000 dunams of land under control via armed settlers by July 2026.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that the documentary Naza is based on blood libels, deliberate distortions of reality, and grave false accusations against Israeli soldiers and the IDF
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Israeli directors portraying the Israeli military as war criminals receive applause at the Venice festival.
The film Naza was produced by the UK's Guardian newspaper.
Israeli strikes killed at least two people and destroyed tents in Gaza on 14 September.
Israeli warplanes killed a family of four in Beit Lahia on 10 September.
A drone strike near Sumoud camp in Khan Younis killed Jihad Ismail on 11 September.
A pregnant woman, Iman Shalouf, died from wounds sustained days earlier on 12 September.
A Palestinian was killed by Israeli gunfire in al-Mawasi, Rafah on 14 September.
Gaza’s Ministry of Health reported 73,786 killed and 174,771 wounded on 14 September.
Al-Ahli Arab Hospital suspended its imaging department due to a failed generator on 13 September.
Gaza’s bus operators’ union announced a suspension of transport for doctors and nurses on 13 September.
Israel approved only 13,445 litres of engine oil against 93,000 pending requests since March.
Twelve countries announced sanctions on Israeli settlement goods on 8 September.
Israel ordered the UK to close its consulate in East Jerusalem on 9 September.
Israel barred 12 British public figures, including 11 MPs, on 9 September.
